summary: Moon Plan B is a web tool that shows, hour by hour for 2026–2030, when a lunar landing site can see the Sun and when it has a direct line of sight to Earth. It uses NASA LOLA elevation data to model the local horizon where terrain coverage is available, and JPL Horizons and NAIF SPICE for Sun and Earth positions. Planners can compare 23 locations, see the Sun and Earth against the horizon in 2D and 3D, and, if a launch slips, find later landing dates with enough hours of visibility (“Plan B”). We checked the results against NASA illumination maps.
details:
• How it works: Our Python engine, lunarnav, compares the Sun and Earth with the horizon that a 2 m mast would see. The default run (B2) uses NASA NAIF SPICE for their positions and NASA Goddard’s LOLA elevation models for terrain. A second run (A2) uses JPL Horizons and Moon Trek. Where terrain is available, the engine accounts for lunar curvature and checks the horizon in 720 directions out to 150 km.
  • Using the planner: Choose a UTC date range and rank the 23 locations by hours with the Sun, Earth or both in view. Compare two locations or two dates, inspect the horizon in 2D and 3D, and check the longest stretch of darkness or loss of Earth visibility. If a launch slips, Plan B searches later landing dates for windows that meet the selected visibility criteria. The English and Vietnamese interface includes an AI guide, shareable links, CSV and JSON downloads, and printable reports. Authorized team members can also request calculations for custom coordinates.
  • Validation: Across six test sites, the largest difference in the apparent directions from Horizons and SPICE was 0.002 arcseconds. In a separate 18.6-year comparison with NASA Goddard’s illumination maps, all 30 permanently shadowed test pixels had zero modeled sunlight. For 30 well-lit pixels, the 2 m model differed from the NASA map by a median of 3.9 percentage points in absolute terms (r = 0.90). A surface-level test gave a larger median difference of 6.3 points.
  • Limits: Hourly sampling can miss short events between samples. Five of the 23 locations lack terrain coverage in B2 and use a smooth-sphere horizon, so nearby terrain could block more of the sky. Estimating actual power output or radio link quality requires additional information about the lander and its equipment.
  • Software: A Node.js API built with Fastify serves the results from MongoDB to the Next.js planner. Public API explorer  https://lunavigator.com/api-docs
  • Source code  https://github.com/justsomenewbie/moon-plan-b
